title: Awards Season Heats Up With ‘The Only Living Pickpocket In New York,’ ‘Fatherland’ & More – Specialty Preview
full_text: Skip to main content By Jill Goldsmith Jill Goldsmith Co-Business Editor More Stories By Jill Abramorama Takes North America Rights, Sets Release For John David Coles Doc ‘The Choice’ Mayor Zohran Mamdani And Neon Set Free NYC Screenings Of ‘Once Upon A Time In Harlem’ Elon Musk Steps In With $1 Billion Equity Investment For Debt-Laden Skydance — Report View All October 23, 2026 5:30pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source L-R: 'The Only Living Pickpocket in New York', 'Wicker', 'Fatherland' and 'A Talent for Murder' Sony PIctures Classics/Black Bear Pictures/Mubi/Bleecker Street The weekend feels awards-y with John Turturro tugging the heartstrings in The Only Living Pickpocket in New York , Olivia Colman ( Wicker ) and Helen Mirren ( A Talent For Murder ) in the house, and Hans Zischler and Sandra Hüller playing Thomas Mann and his daughter on a road trip ( Fatherland ). The A24 You Can See Everything phenomenon goes wide, and Netflix expands its TIFF audience award-winner La Bola Negra . Sony Pictures Classics opens the Turturro-starring Pickpocket by Noah Segan in limited release on six screens in New York (AMC Lincoln Square, Angelika Film Center, Bam Rose) and Los Angeles (AMC Burbank, AMC Grove, Laemmle Royal). He plays Harry Lehman, an aging pickpocket who plies his trade with ever-diminishing returns in a drastically changed New York. Related Stories Reviews Deadline’s Reviews Of This Week’s Box Office Openers: ‘Clayface’, ‘Wildwood’ & More News ‘Clayface’ Takes Shape As No. 1 With $23M-$25M; ‘You Can See Everything’s Wild Ride Continues With $19M – Box Office Update Turturro took the Zurich Film Festival’s Golden Eye Award for his performance in the film — Segan’s directorial debut. Steve Buscemi as Harry’s regular fence; Tatiana Maslany as his estranged daughter; and Will Price as the arrogant, heat-packing scion of a Manhattan crime family also star. A favorite out of Sundance where it premiered, the film is Rotten Tomatoes Certified Fresh at 97% . See Deadline’s review , which calls it mesmerizing. Watch on Deadline Mubi is out with Paweł Pawlikowski’s Fatherland , also limited, at four theaters in New York (Film Forum, Film at Lincoln Center) and Los Angeles (AMC Burbank, Laemmle Royal). World premiered at Cannes to critical acclaim and the Best Director award for Pawlikowski. At 91% Certified Fresh on Rotten Tomatoes, see Deadline review . In the summer of 1949, at the height of the Cold War, Nobel Prize-winning writer Thomas Mann (Zischler) and his daughter Erika (Hüller) embark on a challenging and emotional road trip across a Germany in ruins, from U.S.-dominated Frankfurt to Soviet-controlled Weimar. Mann, who had returned home after 16 years in exile in the U.S., faced not only a divided fatherland but also a deep fracture within his own family. Pawlikowski picks up here where he left off with his award-winning Ida and Cold War , exploring themes of identity, family, love and guilt amid the turmoil and confusion of post-war Europe. Mubi also debuts Making Marie Antoinette , the late filmmaker Eleanor Coppola’s behind-the-scenes documentation of her daughter Sofia Coppola directing 2006 film Marie Antoinette . Premiered at Telluride, Deadline review here . Opens on 20 screens nationally including NY and L.A. Moderate/wide Bleecker Street, in partnership with longtime collaborator LD Entertainment, releases Anton Corbijn thriller A Talent For Murder on 876 screens with Helen Mirren starring as celebrated crime novelist Patricia Highsmith. World premiered at TIFF, see Deadline review. Based on Joanna Murray-Smith’s acclaimed 2014 play Switzerland , the film follows a young literary agent from New York (Alden Ehrenreich), who travels to Switzerland on a mission to convince the famously reclusive Highsmith to write one final installment in her iconic Ripley series. What begins as a seemingly straightforward assignment soon takes an unexpected turn. Black Bear launches Wicker , the Sundance breakout from Eleanor Wilson and Alex Huston Fischer, at 1,471 theaters. A lusty comedic fable about sex, marriage and social convention centered around a lonely Fisherwoman (Colman), who commissions a wicker husband from the local Basketmaker (Peter Dinklage). Her unexpected romance with the creation (Alexander Skarsgård) sparks jealousy and threatens the village’s social order. The Tailor’s Wife/bullying local queen bee (Elizabeth Debicki) sets out to sabotage the romance. Rotten Tomatoes Certified Fresh at 92% with critics. Audience score of 93%. Deadline review here .

title: ‘Street Fighter’ Breakout Callina Liang Talks Embracing Fan Skepticism and Reveals Two Key Scrapped Moments
full_text: × Skip to main content By Brian Davids Plus Icon Brian Davids Writer PickYourBrian Follow Sign Up View All October 23, 2026 4:53pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source Emma McIntyre/Getty Images for SiriusXM Logo text [This story contains spoilers for Street Fighter .] When Street Fighter star Callina Liang was cast as Chun-Li, one of her all-time favorite video game characters, she understood the fans’ skepticism. In fact, she shared their concerns that her physique didn’t yet match that of the beloved martial artist, whom many consider the most iconic female character in fighting games. She didn’t take the criticism personally, but she still used it as bulletin board material to hopefully win over her doubters. “A lot of the comments I read online motivated me even more to prove them wrong. But I agree that, physically, where I started wasn’t where I would ideally want Chun-Li to be,” Liang tells The Hollywood Reporter . Related Stories Movies 'Street Fighter' Director Kitao Sakurai Built a Career by Embracing the Ridiculous Movies 'You Can See Everything' Triumphs With $15M as 'Street Fighter' Wins Weekend From that moment on, Liang went all-in on becoming the beloved fighter, putting herself through an intense physical transformation to embody the undercover Interpol agent. She pumped iron multiple times a week, trained in stunts and martial arts daily and followed a rigorous diet that included 12 eggs per day. For a character whose martial arts style is defined by her powerful kicks, Liang added nearly three inches to her thighs. The physical overhaul was so dramatic that her stunt double had to wear “butt pads” to mirror Liang’s new figure whenever they swapped in and out of scenes. It’s a staggering metamorphosis, particularly for anyone familiar with the Canadian-Chinese actor’s previous roles as high school girls exploited by their classmates in Steven Soderbergh’s Presence and J.C. Lee’s Bad Genius . “Honestly, I wasn’t expecting [my legs to keep growing], but the amazing crafty table they had on set definitely helped,” Liang says. “I definitely felt the pressure. I just didn’t want to disappoint anyone.” Chun-Li infiltrates Lord M. Bison’s (David Dastmalchian) criminal and military organization to avenge her father’s murder at the hands of the Shadaloo leader. At the same time, Bison seeks to lure Ryu (Andrew Koji) into his second World Warrior tournament, where he plans to siphon the reigning champion’s psycho power for himself. Chun-Li helps track down Ken Masters’ (Noah Centineo) estranged adoptive brother, further ingratiating herself with Bison until he offers to formally welcome her into Shadaloo. In an earlier version of the script, Chun-Li was meant to sacrifice a finger as part of this initiation and show of loyalty to Bison’s syndicate, but Capcom, the creators of the Street Fighter video game franchise, appeared to take issue with the idea. The hesitation is understandable, especially when you consider the practical complications that could arise if sequels or spinoffs are to follow. It’s a similar predicament to the one filmmaker Chad Stahelski and Keanu Reeves encountered with John Wick’s own act of fealty in John Wick: Chapter 3 – Parabellum . The assassin ultimately cut off his own finger, forcing the filmmakers to account for its absence in every subsequent shot of Chapter 3 , Chapter 4 and Ballerina , including the added VFX costs of digitally removing it. The compromise for Chun-Li was considerably less drastic. Instead of sacrificing a digit, she receives the mark of Shadaloo on her inner palm. “Chun-Li was originally supposed to chop off a finger, but Capcom … They went back and forth with the script, and eventually they decided that hand-branding was the better way to do it,” Liang shares. “If she had no pinky for the rest of the [potential series], it would be deforming the character in a way.” Getting into spoiler territory, Liang admits she was a little frustrated that Chun-Li didn’t get to fulfill her mission of taking down Bison. “Honestly, a little bit,” Liang says when asked if she was disappointed. “The whole film, especially Chun-Li’s storyline, builds toward Chun-Li’s final takedown of Bison. But there’s a reason for everything, and hopefully, if we get a sequel one day, we’ll get to explore that. I’m sure it’d be epic.” During a scene in which Chun-Li tries to wake Ken up to the fact that the tournament is merely a front for draining the power of his former best friend and training partner, Ryu, another creative choice wound up on the cutting-room floor. Dating back to her chemistry read with Centineo, Liang suggested slapping Ken, and her co-star encouraged her to truly go for the jugular. But despite filming the moment on set, the genuine slap ultimately fell by the wayside. “On the day, we actually tried multiple takes where I physically slapped him across the face,” Liang says. “There was no way to really fake it, so Noah just let me slap him in the face a couple of times. It didn’t end up making it into the final cut, but it was fun.” Below, in a conversation with THR , Liang also discusses the “Tuesday” homage to Raul Julia’s M. Bison in 1994’s Street Fighter , as well as turning Chun-Li’s infamous shower scene from Street Fighter II: The Animated Movie into an amusing gag. *** Callina Liang stars as Chloe in Steven Soderbergh’s Presence Courtesy of Sundance Institute I first saw you in Presence , and while it’s not easy to make single-location movies compelling, you guys pulled it off. Did you feel a career bump after that? Did it perhaps open the door to Street Fighter ? Presence definitely opened a lot of doors for me, but I don’t know if it directly connected to me getting Street Fighter . I started auditioning for Street Fighter two years after we finished Presence , so it had been a while. When I first connected with [Legendary Pictures producer] Cale [Boyter], I remember he was like, “No, I haven’t seen Presence .” Maybe he finally watched it after meeting me. But working with Steven Soderbergh was a huge honor, and I learned so much from being on set with him. Most of my scenes, as Chloe, were with the ghost, and the ghost was essentially the camera with Steven as the DoP. So a lot of it was mainly just me and Steven interacting with each other. It truly felt like a masterclass in cinematography. On the first day, Steven said to the cast, “I’m going to go all-in. It’s risky to make a movie like this. There’s only one way it’s going to go. It either works or it doesn’t, and we just all have to trust that it’s going to work.” And it ended up working. You got a call from your reps about auditioning for Chun-Li in Street Fighter , starting with a Zoom call with director Kitao Sakurai and producer Cale Boyter. Afterwards, they signaled to your agent that you were probably dead in the water, but you kept getting called back — to the point that you had to bail on your birthday plans with your friends to fly out for a chemistry read with Noah Centineo. Have your pals finally forgiven you for choosing career advancement over them? ( Laughs .) Oh, absolutely. If any of my friends were unwilling to forgive me, then they weren’t a real one to begin with. It was a crazy ride, and honestly, it was the best birthday present I could have ever asked for. A couple days after I got back from the chemistry read with Noah in L.A., Kitao called me personally to tell me that I got the role of Chun-Li. So it was a dream come true, and there was no better way I would’ve spent my birthday. Callina Liang’s Chun-Li and Noah Centineo’s Ken Masters in Street Fighter Courtesy of Paramount Pictures And Legendary Pictures Did you and Noah read the bathroom scene where she warns Ken that the tournament is a front to steal Ryu’s power? We did the scene where Chun-Li invites Ken to the tournament, and then we did the scene of us together in the bathroom. In the chemistry read, Cale sat in on some of it, but it was mostly me, Noah and Kitao working together. At some point, Kitao was like, “To get Ken to see that the tournament is not a real thing, I think Chun-Li would get physical. Do you think you can add some physicality to it?” And I was like, “Noah, are you comfortable with this?” And he was like, “Sure, go ahead.” And I was like, “Alright, if I have the green light.” So for one of the takes, I grabbed him by the collar and slapped him across the face, saying, “Wake up! This is not a real tournament.” It was so much fun. Then we brought Cale in to watch it, and he was like, “Oh my gosh, I wasn’t expecting that. That was great.” On the day, we actually tried multiple takes where I physically slapped him across the face. There was no way to really fake it, so Noah just let me slap him in the face a couple of times. It didn’t end up making it into the final cut, but it was fun. There’s a video of you guys promoting the movie somewhere, and Noah suddenly jumped on the game-inspired car that was there, giving you quite a jump-scare. What’s your version of that story? ComplexCon was a lot of fun, but hectic. We were up on this stage with an audience of people watching, and all I could think in my head was that I was wearing these six-inch heels with insane platforms. They looked amazing with my outfit. My stylists, Wayman and Micah, kill it every single time. But I was just trying my hardest to stay balanced and not fall over while we were taking pictures and filming content around that car in front of the crowd that gathered at our stand. Then Noah jumped on the car, but I’m honestly used to it. Working with Noah and [Andrew] Koji, they always pretend to fight each other or jump on things, on and off set. So I was mostly just like, Oh my gosh, I can’t fall over. Not right now. But other than that, I was like, Oh, it’s just Noah being Noah . I didn’t end up falling over, and all was good. But I was concerned about his shoulder. I actually asked him afterwards if he hurt it, and he said he didn’t. Callina Liang’s Chun-Li in Street Fighter Courtesy of Paramount Pictures And Legendary Pictures Back to pre-production, you had two months to get jacked, particularly your legs, since Chun-Li is known for her dangerous kicks. Was it a sprint to the finish line? Yeah, absolutely. I sprinted all the way. Even after filming had started, I kept going to weightlifting sessions whenever my schedule allowed it. Stunt training also kept going all throughout. I learned the first choreo I had to film, and then after we filmed that, I had to learn the second choreo I had to film. So I kept up with the eating, and that’s why my legs kept growing from the first day of filming to the last day of filming. Honestly, I wasn’t expecting it, but the amazing crafty table they had on set definitely helped. So I definitely felt the pressure of time, the expectations of longtime fans and the expectations I had of myself. I just didn’t want to disappoint anyone. So it’s true that you used the fan response to your casting as bulletin board material? Yeah, it really was motivation. A lot of the comments I read online just motivated me even more to prove them wrong, but nothing really got to me personally. I was like, Listen, I agree with you guys. As an outsider who’s also a fan of the games and the character, I agree that, physically, where I started wasn’t where I would ideally want Chun-Li to be. But there’s always room for growth. You can always be better, and that’s the way I looked at it. The Street Fighter cast is such an odd collection of people. You have wrestlers, a rapper, a real-life vampire, a few comedians, a country musician, a bodybuilder and several martial artists. Was the set basically a rambunctious carnival? Yes, absolutely. There’s really no better way to put it. There was never a dull moment on set. Every day was chaotic, but chaotic in a fun way. I was personally fangirling over 50 Cent whenever he was on set. Eric André and Schulz were always making jokes and filming prank videos. I was always confused by them, but I ended up laughing along with them. I was actually really intimidated by the wrestlers at first. Who wouldn’t be? You have Roman Reigns and Cody Rhodes, and what they do looks scary. But they ended up being the sweetest people. They’re such puppies in the best way, and they were super nice to hang around with on set. And Orville Peck has become one of my best friends after filming this whole thing together. David [Dastmalchian] is a real-life vampire, for sure, but in the best way. It was magnificent working with him and diving into the psychology of Bison and Chun-Li. We got to do some of the more serious stuff, which excited me a lot personally. But it was a crazy set. You had your crazy uncles and aunties and cousins, and it genuinely felt like one big, crazy family. Callina Liang’s Chun-Li in Street Fighter Paramount Pictures There’s an amazing sight gag in this film after Chun-Li does some drunken nunchucking. She goes to take a shower, and just as she’s about to be revealed, the movie match-cuts to E. Honda’s exposed upper body. Was this gag scripted carefully so that you knew what to expect? ( Laughs. ) It was scripted from day one. Kitao sent me a mock-up about a week before we filmed it, showing exactly how they were planning to shoot it, including the push-in and reveal of E. Honda’s big chest. I was made to feel very comfortable from the start, and I knew exactly what I was stepping into on the day. So I was very happy to do it because it’s such an iconic scene from Street Fighter II: The Animated Movie . As a fan myself, that’s probably my favorite movie in the franchise, so I was like, “We’ve got to add that Easter egg in there.” And now it’s gotten big laughs at all the screenings. Audiences have loved it. Even I laughed when I first saw it. Chun-Li is an undercover Interpol officer, and she infiltrates M. Bison’s organization as part of her long-running effort to avenge her father’s murder at his hand. She then brands herself with his Shadaloo symbol to prove her loyalty. Did they do anything on the day to give you some kind of sensation you could play off? No, actually. That scene used to be something else. I don’t know if I’m allowed to say this, but the movie is out now, so it should be fine. Chun-Li was originally supposed to chop off a finger, but Capcom … They went back and forth with the script, and eventually they decided that hand-branding was the better way to do it. I remember testing that scene during the camera test. I tried it, and I thought, It’s a lot. She’s about to physically hurt herself . But Kitao kept going, “More, more, more. I want to see it in her eyes. She’s almost shaking.” And I was like, “Alright, say less.” So, on the day, I mentally channeled whatever pain I could into what was happening physically. But I wish there had been something to help me feel that sensation. It was all just stone-cold acting. There was a lot of rigamarole with the studio over Keanu Reeves, as John Wick, cutting off a finger in the John Wick series, so that’s an interesting yet familiar story. I wonder if that’s where the inspiration came from. If she had no pinky for the rest of the [potential series], it would be deforming the character in a way. But regardless, I think the hand-branding worked, and it was very fun to play. Kitao told me that the reasoning came down to the source material being too substantial to cram it all into one movie, but were you disappointed at all that Chun-Li didn’t get to take out M. Bison in this film? Oh, man. Honestly, a little bit. The whole film, especially Chun-Li’s storyline, builds toward Chun-Li’s final takedown of Bison. But there’s a reason for everything, and hopefully, if we get a sequel one day, we’ll get to explore that. I’m sure it’d be epic. Callina Liang’s Chun-Li and David Dastmalchian’s Lord M. Bison in Street Fighter Courtesy of Paramount Pictures And Legendary Pictures You made a good point elsewhere that if she does kill him, who is she after that? She’s devoted her entire life toward this one mission. Exactly. That’s another part of her storyline and character arc I’d be interested to explore. Whenever I went into my scenes with Bison in this film, I had to tap into this weird mental state of hating him so much, but finding comfort in knowing exactly what Chun-Li needed to do, who she hated and what her mission was. Even in the moments before she brands herself, he says, “There’s a deep sadness in you and also a great potential.” I almost felt emotional as her during those moments. It’s almost the first time anyone has truly seen Chun-Li for who she is, so there’s a weird sense of emotional support in that moment. After she brands herself, he brings her up close to the painting of himself, which is hilarious. She could have easily chosen to attack him when he hands her the knife while standing that close to him, but she chose not to. So that’s really interesting to think about because she probably didn’t want her mission to end just yet. She was probably afraid to confront what would come for her, mentally, once it was all over. So I 100 percent don’t know how she’d feel after finally accomplishing Bison’s death. Maybe you weren’t there for David Dastmalchian’s coverage after Bison hits Chun-Li with the Psycho Crusher, but was there a lot of pomp and circumstance around his “Tuesday” homage to Raul Julia as he walks from her? Oh my gosh, absolutely. It’s the most iconic line ever. Even before filming started, we were all saying, “We’ve got to put that line in there somehow. We’ve got to find the right moment.” Then I saw the dailies where he delivered that line, and I was like, “Damn, that’s the one.” It was so satisfying to watch, and then it became a thing the rest of the shoot. He shot the line earlier on in the filming process, and every day afterwards, whenever we’d see each other, I’d be like, “Yeah, I’m going to kill you today.” I was just gearing up to fight him. But David was like, “Hey, it’s just a Tuesday for me.” So that iconic line became an ongoing joke between us. Callina Liang’s Chun-Li and Kyle Mooney’s Marvin in Street Fighter Courtesy of Paramount Pictures And Legendary Pictures Decades from now, when you look back on this experience, what day will you likely recall first? The one day that always stands out to me was when we filmed on that beautiful cliffside in Sydney. Chun-Li invites Dhalsim to the tournament, and it was just truly so beautiful. I could not believe we were filming at a location like that. After the part on the rocks, where Dhalism and his soldiers are doing their thing, we moved on to another oceanside cliff where the chopper is. Chun-Li has this crazy fight sequence with three of her Interpol bosses, and then kicking [Kyle Mooney’s] Marvin in the balls was the end of that day. So it was such a beautiful day. I got to fight three guys, kick another one in the balls and drive off in a van. It was a great day. I’ll never forget it. I wonder if it was a Tuesday. It might have been a Tuesday! *** Street Fighter is now playing in movie theaters . THR

title: All The Songs In ‘Klara And The Sun’: Violent Femmes & More
full_text: Skip to main content By Dessi Gomez Dessi Gomez SEO Staff Writer @GomezDessi More Stories By Dessi Everything We Know About Universal’s ‘Miami Vice ’85’ Movie So Far All The Songs In ‘Klara And The Sun’: Violent Femmes & More All The Songs In Laika’s ‘Wildwood’: From Portugal. The Man To The Decemberists View All October 23, 2026 4:34pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source L-R: Mia Tharia and Jenna Ortega star in 'Klara and the Sun' Sony 3000 Pictures Taika Waititi ’s Klara and the Sun , based on the book by Kazuo Ishiguro, stars Jenna Ortega as the titular robotic Artificial Friend. The film follows Klara as she wishes for a charge or owner to claim her from the Friend Store, where she gets a limited amount of time in the front alcove to show off and garner attention. Then she is chosen by Josie (Mia Tharia), whose mother Chrissy ( Amy Adams ) is reluctant to purchase an older model of the product when the newer ones are being sold at Fancy Friends down the street. But Klara and Josie’s bond is solid from the moment they meet eye contact. title: Nick Reiner’s Push for Release of Trust Money to Be Decided by Mediator
full_text: × Skip to main content By Winston Cho Plus Icon Winston Cho View All October 23, 2026 4:26pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source Nick Reiner appears with Deputy Public Defender Kimberly Greene during his arraignment in Los Angeles County Superior Court on Feb. 23, 2026. Chris Torres-Pool/Getty Images A deal has been struck between lawyers for Nick Reiner and the trust allowing a mediator to decide whether he can access funds set aside for him by his parents. The mediation could open the door for him to rehire Alan Jackson, who has represented Harvey Weinstein and Karen Read, among others, and withdrew from the case because of Reiner’s financial constraints. “A criminal defendant has a constitutional right to use money that is lawfully his own to be defended by the lawyer he chooses,” Reiner’s lawyer, Anita Wu, said in a statement. “These issues need to get resolved as quickly as possible.” Related Stories General News Jamie Lee Curtis Leaning on "Love and Service" in Honoring the Late Rob and Michele Reiner: "Every Day With Them Was Activism" Lifestyle Jamie Lee Curtis to Receive Inaugural Award Inspired by Rob and Michele Reiner at Children's Institute Gala; John Mayer to Perform Reiner has been held in custody without bail since pleading not guilty to the murders in February. He was initially charged with two counts of first-degree murder with special circumstances relating to multiple homicides, meaning the maximum sentence he faces is life without parole. The Los Angeles County district attorney’s office has said it will not seek the death penalty after consulting Reiner’s siblings. The trust’s fiduciaries have maintained that Reiner is barred from accessing money in the trust, citing California’s so-called slayer statute. The law prohibits people from receiving an inheritance from those they kill. One issue in the case is whether the statute applies since Reiner hasn’t been convicted. Another is whether the money is already his since half of the funds should’ve been dispersed to him on his 30th birthday in 2023. Under the terms of the irrevocable trust, the other half is to be paid to him when he turns 35. Money from the trust is currently being used to pay for lawyers on both side of the litigation, including those trying to prevent Reiner from accessing the funds. So far, fiduciaries have paid lawyers more than $250,000, according to court filings. The figure is nearly half of the trust, $558,000, Reiner should’ve received when he turned 30. “None of that makes any sense, or serves anyone’s interests,” Wu said. The mediation will begin in December. In court filings, Reiner’s lawyers have also argued that a “substantial portion” of the disputed funds in the trust, at least $325,000, is money from his grandfather, Carl Reiner, who died in 2020. “Nick is not accused of causing his death,” the filing stated. “Money that was left to Nick by his grandfather is not money received by Nick from or through his parents. To the extent the funds Nick received from his grandfather are Nick’s personal assets, they remain Nick’s and should be segregated and released from this trust. Even if they were properly held by the trust, the ‘Slayer Statute’ does not supply a basis for withholding them.” THR

title: Ken Atchity, Producer on ‘Joe Somebody’ and ‘The Meg,’ Dies at 82
full_text: Skip to main content By Mike Barnes Plus Icon Mike Barnes Senior Editor mikebarnes4 Follow Sign Up View All October 23, 2026 4:12pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source Ken Atchity Courtesy of The Blaine Group Ken Atchity, an author and professor who became a literary manager and producer on such films as Joe Somebody , Hysteria and The Meg , has died. He was 82. Atchity died Monday of kidney failure at Cedars-Sinai Medical Center in Los Angeles, his longtime business and producing partner, Chi-Li Wong, told The Hollywood Reporter . Atchity also was behind 16 romantic telefilms made under the banner of Shades of Love that were produced for cable and video. They ran in Canada and on HBO/Cinemax in the States and were released internationally by Warner Bros. Related Stories TV Michael Gray, Former Teen Idol and Star of 'Shazam!,' Dies at 75 Movies Tom Skerritt, Star of 'Picket Fences' and 'Alien,' Dies at 93 Atchity produced the shark thriller The Meg (2018) and its sequel, Meg 2: The Trench (2023), both starring Jason Statham. (Jon Turteltaub directed the first installment, Ben Wheatley the second.) In addition to Joe Somebody (2001), starring Tim Allen, and Hysteria (2011), starring Maggie Gyllenhaal, Atchity produced features including Life or Something Like It (2002), starring Angelina Jolie, and Gospel Hill (2008), directed by Giancarlo Esposito. Other producing credits included the 1989 telefilm The Amityville Horror: The Evil Escapes and the 2010 documentary The Kennedy Detail . An author of more than 20 books, Atchity headed Story Merchant Books, selling his clients’ work to publishers and to film and television outlets while publishing many other works himself. One of five kids, Kenneth John Atchity was born on Jan. 16, 1944, in Eunice, Louisiana. Raised in Kansas City, Missouri, he graduated from Rockhurst High School with an Ignatian Scholarship to study at Georgetown University (while in high school, he published his first book reviews for The Kansas City Star ). At Georgetown, Atchity majored in Classics and English, served as editor-in-chief of the student-run newspaper The Hoya and spent his junior summer at Cambridge University in England, studying literature and social institutions. While earning his master’s degree at Yale, he studied under A. Bartlett Giamatti and Erich Segal, then taught for more than a decade at Occidental College in L.A. before getting into show business in the 1980s. Survivors include his wife, Kayoko, whom he married in 2003; his children, Vincent and Rosemary; his grandchildren, Margaret, Edward, Oliver, Eliot and Louis; and his sisters, Mary and Laurie. Donations in his memory can be made Yoga Gives Back , which aims to empower women and children in India. THR

title: Marysa Maslansky, Founder of the Renowned Visages Photo Agency, Dies at 82
full_text: Skip to main content By Mike Barnes Plus Icon Mike Barnes Senior Editor mikebarnes4 Follow Sign Up View All October 23, 2026 3:44pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source Marysa Maslansky Davis Factor Marysa Maslansky, whose influential Visages Photo Agency represented such A-list photographers as Herb Ritts, Mary Ellen Mark and George Hurrell in the 1980s and ’90s, has died. She was 82. Maslansky died Oct. 9 at her home in Los Angeles after a long illness, a family spokesperson announced. Born in Pas-de-Calais, France, on April 27, 1944, Maslansky settled in Los Angeles in 1969 and worked as a journalist for the Sygma Photo News agency before heading Gamma Liaison, the L.A. branch of Gamma, the prominent French photo agency. Related Stories TV Michael Gray, Former Teen Idol and Star of 'Shazam!,' Dies at 75 Movies Tom Skerritt, Star of 'Picket Fences' and 'Alien,' Dies at 93 In 1980, she founded Visages, and in addition to Ritts, Mark and Hurrell, the agency would become home to many other iconic celebrity and fashion photographers, among them William Claxton, Greg Gorman, Matthew Rolston, Paul Jasmin, Sofia Coppola, Brad Branson and Firooz Zahedi. When Ritts started with Maslansky at Visages, his fee was in the range of $750 a day, the Los Angeles Times wrote back then. But by 1990, he was earning about $20,000 a day as one of the highest-paid commercial photographers in the U.S. at the time. Visages closed its doors in 2000 amid the shift to digital, industry consolidation and competition from major syndicates including Getty Images and Corbis. Maslansky was married to Michael Maslansky — a founding partner (with Pat Kingsley and Neil Koenigsberg) of what would become PMK Public Relations — from 1975 until his death in 1993 of stroke complications at age 55. His clients included Goldie Hawn, Sylvester Stallone, Liza Minnelli and Katharine Hepburn . Survivors include her second husband, Christopher, son Max and daughter-in-law Nancy. Another son, Alex, died in 2023 at age 43. THR

title: Ethan Klein Says He’s Working to “Urgently Remove My Ownership, Financial Stakes” From H3 Podcast After Wife Hila Klein Reveals His Affair

Matt Winkelmeyer/Getty Images YouTuber Ethan Klein has been dropped from the popular H3 Podcast after his wife Hila Klein revealed that he has been having an affair for over six months, and he’s breaking his silence on the allegations. “We are all shocked, angry, and heartbroken to learn about Ethan’s ongoing affair. As soon as we found out, we all agreed: we would not continue working with Ethan involved or profiting in any way,” the H3 Podcast crew wrote on Instagram late Thursday. “We don’t yet know what that means for the future. There’s a lot to work through, and we wish we had more answers for you.” Related Stories Movies 'The Telepathy Tapes' Movie Based on Podcast Lands at Amazon MGM for Early 2027 Release (Exclusive) News Rupert Grint Sets Next Project: Noiser Audiobook Adaptation of 'Treasure Island' (Exclusive) The statement continued, “We stand with Hila and will support her every step of the way. We’re disgusted by Ethan’s actions and the hurt he has caused. We all deserved better: Hila, us, and you. “Please know that we’re safe, we’re sticking together, and we’re looking after each other. We’ve put so much of ourselves into this show, and it’s hard to find the words for what we’re feeling right now. Thank you for giving us some time to figure things out, and for all the love you’ve shown us. We love you, and we miss you already.” Ethan and Hila co-host H3 on their YouTube channel, which has amassed 2.5 million followers. Ethan previously co-hosted the Frenemies podcast (which aired on H3 ‘s YouTube) alongside Trisha Paytas, whom is married to Hila’s brother Moses Hacmon; they canceled that podcast after a fallout. Ethan shared an initial statement on his Instagram Story Friday asking fans to “please respect my family’s privacy and do not contact them looking for me or asking for their comments. They have nothing to do with this and share in your outrage and disappointment. Thank you.” He then shared a follow-up post when he confirmed he’s in the process of fully cutting ties with the H3 Podcast . “I am working with Hila to urgently remove my ownership and financial stakes in any podcasts, [Hila’s businesses] Teddy Fresh, Teddy Glow or any joint venture that I would profit from. All of your support will go directly to Hila and the crew,” Ethan wrote. “I do this in the hope that people can still support Hila and the Crew without the concern of enriching me. I know the crew will make an awesome show, they are packed to the brim with the most talented, creative, hilarious and all around great people.” Hila shared on Instagram late Thursday night that she learned her husband, Ethan, had been having an affair. She wrote, “I am living a nightmare I can’t wake up from. My husband has been having an affair. I have been fed lie after lie after lie for months. Here is the truth.” “I could sense something was wrong. I tried to ask him questions and share my concerns and hurt feelings. But I was met with dismissive answers and no action. Things that bothered me continued to bother me, and he did nothing about it. So I trusted him. Because I loved him. I stopped questioning him and began to question myself, my own instincts. My sanity,” she continued. “Eventually, he was caught in a lie, and I knew I was done. But the lies continued. ‘It was just a kiss’ became ‘it was emotional cheating.’ After I dragged these lies from him, he finally admitted he’d been in an affair for over 6 months, the extent of which I’m sure I still don’t know.” Hila wrote, “The betrayal I feel is immeasurable. The person I loved and trusted for 20 years evaporated overnight. He was my safe place, my partner in marriage, parenting, and business. My only family on this side of the world. How do I even begin to make sense of this?” “I don’t know what comes next; I’ve never been here before. I am in survival mode, trying to navigate separation, co-parenting, and unthinkable heartbreak. All I can do right now is focus on taking care of myself and my children, one day at a time. You’re not crazy. Trust your instincts. Trust yourself. If you’re not being treated right, get up and leave,” she concluded. The H3 Podcast launched in 2016 and has featured interviews with Post Malone, MrBeast and Jack Black. It’s been nominated for best podcast at the Streamy Awards five times. Ethan and Hila married in 2012, and share three children. THR

title: Chappell Roan Enlists PinkPantheress to Close Out Super Graphic Spectacular Fundraising Shows

The two-day event, held at the Shrine Auditorium and Expo Hall, was billed as a fundraising event featuring live performances, volunteer opportunities, connection and a special headlining set from Roan herself. Roan was preceded by sets from Polachek, Muna, Alisa Mae, Fantasia Royale Gaga and Sweat Eddie. With a block party that kicked off in the afternoon, the event, which raised money for the pop star’s foundation The Midwest Princess Project, which supports trans youth and the LGBTQ+ community. All proceeds of the event were donated to the organization. Related Stories Movies Tanner Buchanan, Peyton Elizabeth Lee to Star in 'Gasoline' From 'SLC Punk!' Director James Merendino (Exclusive) Music Victoria Justice on Releasing a Remixed "Love Zombie," a Viral Hit 15 Years in the Making Comedian Caleb Hearon hosted the evening, and even joined MUNA during the band’s set. Roan delivered a high-energy performance to the just over 6,000 capacity room. It was a large underplay for the Rise and Fall of a Midwest Princess singer, who is without-a-doubt a stadium act at this point, having drawn an estimated 40,000 per night at her Pasadena shows last year. The audience for Thursday’s show was just as high-energy back, and an argument could be made that they might be one of the most engaged crowd’s the venue’s ever seen. Roan used every inch of the gothic-themed stage during her roughly 70-minute set, kicking off with, unsurprisingly, “Super Graphic Ultra Modern Girl.” The setlist was consistent with other shows the singer’s done over the past year, leaning heavily on her breakout album The Rise and Fall of a Midwest Princess, with some newer songs — “The Subway,” “Good Luck, Babe!” and “The Giver” — sprinkled in. Chappell Roan and PinkPantheress onstage during The Super Graphic Spectacular. @IZZYNUZZOPHOTO During night one, Christina Aguilera joined Roan, and she sang her her classic hit “Beautiful” before the two singers joined together for a duet of “Coffee.” For night two, Roan mixed things up, bringing out PinkPantheress, describing the British pop star as being “fantastic” and “just so cunt” as she introduced her. PinkPantheress performed “Tonight” for the crowd, while Roan danced around onstage with her band. Later in the show, Roan brought out Lola Young, who performed in one of the opening slots on night one, for a duet of Roan’s “Picture You.” The song, one of Roan’s more underrated offerings, was a highlight of the night. Naturally, Roan brought her signature candor and wit to the performance, joking around with fans in the audience. “There’s some straight people in the front row, I can tell,” she said at one point during the performance before later, during the song, rushing to tell the straight it was OK. It was all in good fun. Roan even dedicated “The Giver,” her lesbian country anthem, to “all the top lesbians out there.” The night ended with a performance of the singer’s remix of the Olivia Rodrigo song “Expectations,” which she performed as a solo, and smash hit “Pink Pony Club.” During the song — which features the lyrics “Won’t make my Mama proud / it’s gonna cause a scene / She sees her baby girl / I know she’s gonna scream” — the singer pointed to the mezzanine to inform the crowd her actual mother was in attendance. The moment got a big cheer from the crowd. “Pink Pony Club” is the type of concert anthem that will never get old, with every person in the room singing the lyrics as loud as they can. All net proceeds from both shows, sponsored by CashApp and Visa, will be donated to the The Midwest Princess Project to power “the next chapter” of the queer-centric organization’s work. THR

title: TV Ratings: ‘Cupertino’ and ‘Line of Fire’ More than Double in Delayed Viewing
full_text: Skip to main content By Rick Porter Plus Icon Rick Porter Television Business Editor rickporter Follow Sign Up View All October 23, 2026 3:02pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source Rachel Keller and Mike Colter in 'Cupertino' (left); Kat Cunning and Peter Krause in 'Line of Fire' Elizabeth Fisher/CBS; Ralph Bavaro/NBC Logo text Cupertino and Line of Fire are very different shows on screen, but their ratings profiles early in the season are very similar. Both shows draw about 3 million viewers for their initial airings (3.03 million for Cupertino’ s first two episodes on CBS, 2.98 million over three for Line of Fire on NBC). That’s not bad for a 10 p.m. network show — it tends to be the least watched hour of primetime — but a few other series that air in that hour are ahead of them. Cupertino and Line of Fire are also picking up a lot of viewing — most of their seven-day totals, in fact — after those initial airings. The 2026-27 TV season is just a month old, so these are necessarily small sample sizes. But if these early patterns hold up, Cupertino and Line of Fire are poised to draw audiences well above their same-day audiences. Related Stories TV Streaming Ratings: 'Carrie' Has a Bloody Good Opening Week TV NBC Extends 'Line of Fire' With Full-Season Pickup CBS’ two other rookies, NCIS: New York and Eternally Yours , also had good starts, with the former’s Oct. 6 series premiere ranking sixth among all network shows (excluding live sports) after a week of cross-platform viewing. The latest entry in the NCIS franchise grew to 10.25 million viewers over a week, according to Nielsen’s multi-platform ratings. That’s up from 5.62 million same-day viewers — a growth of 82 percent. Of the 4.63 million additional viewers for NCIS: New York , 2.45 million came via streaming (about 24 percent of the all-in, seven-day total) and 2.18 million via DVR. Cupertino’ s Oct. 8 premiere more than doubled after a week, going from 3.19 million on-air viewers to 7.17 million. The majority (2.18 million) of its after-air viewers came to the show via DVR, while an additional 1.8 million streamed the premiere in seven days. Through its first three episodes, Line of Fire is averaging 6.9 million cross-platform viewers over a week, also more than doubling its initial audience (2.98 million). Its delayed viewing also tilts a little toward DVR playback (2.08 million viewers) vs. streaming (1.84 million). In announcing a full-season order for the show on Thursday, NBC also noted that the Sept. 21 premiere has grown to 14 million viewers over a month’s time. Eternally Yours , a comedy about a family of vampires, also debuted Oct. 8. It had 4.12 million same-day viewers and 6.94 million after seven days, up 68 percent. About 1.58 million of those were streaming viewers, with 1.24 million coming from DVR playback. Here’s how the four new scripted shows that have premiered so far compare (a fifth, NBC’s comedy Newlyweds , debuts Friday). All figures are through Oct. 11. THR

title: TitledMiami Vice '85
full_text: Skip to main content By Justin Kroll Justin Kroll Film Editor @krolljvar More Stories By Justin Tony Lipp And Dara Gordon Join Entertainment 360 As Partners Cory Michael Smith Joins Scarlett Johansson In ‘Scapegoat’ At Square Peg And A24 Denzel Washington And Christopher McQuarrie Team On New Thriller At United Artists And Amazon MGM Studios View All April 22, 2026 2:00pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source L-R: Michael B Jordan; Philip Michael Thomas and Don Johnson in 'Miami Vice'; and Austin Butler Juan Veloz/Michael Buckner for Deadline/Everett Universal Pictures’ upcoming Miami Vice movie officially has its Tubbs and Crockett as well a title, as Michael B. Jordan and Austin Butler are set to star in Miami Vice ’85 with Joseph Kosinski directing. The film will be shot for Imax and is set to bow on August 6, 2027. The film explores the glamour and corruption of mid-’80s Miami in an all-new version of Miami Vice , inspired by the pilot episode and first season of the landmark Universal Television series that influenced culture and set the style in everything from fashion to filmmaking. Related Stories News Universal Dates Joseph Kosinski’s ‘Miami Vice’ For Late Summer 2027 Casting Austin Butler In Early Talks To Play Sonny Crockett In ‘Miami Vice’ Movie At Universal Deadline reported last fall that Jordan and Butler were in talks to star in the pic, but it was not expected to begin production until fall of 2026, so there was no rush to close deals. Insiders add that the film only recently had its budget greenlighted, and deals for Jordan and Butler closed soon after the studio gave the thumbs up. The film will be produced by Dylan Clark and his Dylan Clark Productions and Kosinski. Nightcrawler Oscar nominee Dan Gilroy is writing the script , based on characters created by Anthony Yerkovich from the series executive produced by Yerkovich and Michael Mann. Eric Warren Singer wrote an earlier draft of the screenplay. Watch on Deadline EVP Production Development Sara Scott and Creative Executive of Production Development Christina Hoffrogge will oversee the project for Universal.
